gaps.title: Peru-Specific ML-Based Milk Collection Optimization
gaps.pain: Generic route optimizers ignore local regulations, road conditions, and spoilage risks unique to Peru, causing inefficiencies and milk waste.
gaps.why_now: Rising milk demand and fuel costs make optimization critical; no local solution yet, and Agil’s Chile model proves demand.
gaps.evidence_needed: Pilot with one cooperative comparing optimized vs. manual routes to measure fuel savings and spoilage reduction.
gaps.risk: Agil may enter Peru and leverage Chile experience; global competitors could add local features.

gaps.title: Affordable Solution for Small Cooperatives
gaps.pain: Small cooperatives cannot afford global tools like Route4Me, forcing them to rely on manual methods that waste time and fuel.
gaps.why_now: Fuel price hikes intensify pain; regulatory traceability requirements pressure modernization, but budgets remain tight.
gaps.evidence_needed: Willingness-to-pay survey and free pilot to demonstrate ROI and adoption willingness.
gaps.risk: Competitors can drop prices or offer freemium; hard to monetize sustainably if target segment is extremely price-sensitive.

gaps.title: Offline-First Mobile App for Remote Milk Collection
gaps.pain: Rural areas lack reliable internet, making real-time optimization useless and forcing drivers to rely on paper and memory, leading to delays and errors.
gaps.why_now: Smartphone penetration is high in rural Peru; offline sync technology is mature and can bridge the connectivity gap.
gaps.evidence_needed: Test offline-capable MVP with drivers in remote regions and compare on-time collection and data accuracy against manual methods.
gaps.risk: Infrastructure may improve faster than expected; offline sync adds development complexity and maintenance overhead.

gaps.title: Integration with Local Farm Management Systems
gaps.pain: Cooperatives use separate tools for farm data and logistics, causing double data entry, errors, and fragmented visibility.
gaps.why_now: Local agtech adoption (e.g., Sismagro, Tambero) is growing, creating an opportunity to be the routing module they lack.
gaps.evidence_needed: Partner with one platform to integrate API and measure reduction in manual data entry and improved planning time.
gaps.risk: Dependency on third-party APIs and partnership delays; competitors could also integrate, reducing uniqueness.

gaps.title: Predictive Routing Based on Milk Quality and Spoilage Risk
gaps.pain: Variable milk quality leads to rejected loads and wasted trips; current routing does not account for spoilage risk or quality grades.
gaps.why_now: Processors demand higher quality and traceability; ML models can now predict spoilage based on weather, distance, and historical data.
gaps.evidence_needed: Build predictive model using historical data from a cooperative and measure reduction in rejected milk and spoilage losses.
gaps.risk: Lack of quality data in small cooperatives; model may not generalize across regions; requires ongoing data collection.

gaps.title: Real-Time Notifications and Dynamic Re-Routing
gaps.pain: Farmers and drivers lack visibility into collection status, causing idle time and uncertainty when delays occur.
gaps.why_now: Real-time tracking is becoming a basic expectation; even WhatsApp is used informally, indicating demand for structured notifications.
gaps.evidence_needed: Implement basic tracking and alert MVP in a pilot and measure farmer/driver satisfaction and reduction in wait times.
gaps.risk: Feature is easy to copy; may not justify a standalone product if not bundled with core optimization; battery/data concerns in remote areas.

checkpoint_instruction: 1. Map connectivity blackspots via field visits and driver interviews in 3 target cooperatives. 2. Build a lightweight offline-first mobile MVP with local route calculation and sync-on-connect. 3. Run a 2-week pilot measuring on-time collection, fuel usage, and driver feedback vs. baseline. 4. Validate willingness to pay at a subscription price point that covers operational costs.
